questions.q: Methyl dodecanoate is treated with one equivalent of DIBAL-H in toluene at −78 °C, followed by H₃O⁺. The products are:
questions.explain: At −78 °C with one equivalent, DIBAL-H reduces the ester only to the aldehyde and releases the alcohol part. Warming or excess reagent gives the 1° alcohol.

questions.q: Benzonitrile is treated with (1) DIBAL-H and (2) H₃O⁺. What is formed, and what would LiAlH₄ give instead?
questions.explain: DIBAL-H delivers one hydride to give an aluminium-bound imine, which work-up hydrolyses to C₆H₅CHO. LiAlH₄ adds two hydrides and gives the primary amine.

questions.q: Why does DIBAL-H stop at the aldehyde when it reduces an ester, while LiAlH₄ goes on to the alcohol?
options: DIBAL-H is a stronger nucleophile than AlH₄⁻
The aldehyde precipitates out of toluene at −78 °C
DIBAL-H cannot reduce aldehydes under any conditions
DIBAL-H has one hydride per Al and, used as one equivalent at −78 °C, is not reactive enough to attack the aldehyde
questions.explain: LiAlH₄ has four reactive hydrides and reduces the intermediate aldehyde faster than the ester. DIBAL-H does reduce aldehydes in general, so temperature and stoichiometry control are essential.

questions.q: Ethyl but-2-enoate is fully reduced with DIBAL-H and worked up. The product is:
questions.explain: DIBAL-H does not reduce an isolated C=C, so full reduction of the α,β-unsaturated ester gives the allylic alcohol with the double bond kept.
